extracted.intended_audience: Naval Contracting Officers and field procurement managers implementing the CITA/A-76 program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for Contracting Officers and procurement organizations on planning, staffing, communications, consolidation, and task-group processes when implementing the CITA (contracting-out) / A-76 acquisition program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CBD notice for non-availability determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing guidance mandates at a minimum the use of a CBD notice in this determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The researcher observes that advertising the requirement in the CBD without simultaneous issuance of a formal solicitation could extend the acquisition by as much as 90 days and may produce little additional beneficial information. The Contracting Officer may be the focal point for determining non-availability of commercial concerns; CBD notice is a minimum required step, but related questions remain largely unanswered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multifunction contracting (combine small functions into larger groupings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine several small in-house functions into larger functional groupings or an 'umbrella' (BOSS) contract so a single contractor provides support for an entire base operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: may reduce total price versus multiple small contracts, lower solicitation preparation and contract administration costs, centralize management and improve communications. Disadvantages: conversion/phase-in and turnover can be turbulent, start-up functions are more difficult due to number of personnel and coordination/communication gaps. Contracting Officers can advise functional activities on grouping functions to enhance single-firm capability; their role is strictly advisory but can be significant if manpower allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of same functions across activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize and centralize review schedule so field activities review the same functions in the same fiscal year and consolidate solicitations for identical services across activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits: coordinated development of work statements and specifications, potential for satisfactory performance under larger contracts (example: San Diego janitorial consolidation). Common problems: little attempt in the field to consolidate, work statements vary from acceptable to poor across activities, coordination difficulties. Causes include conflicting policies encouraging small/disadvantaged business participation (SBA set-asides). Ideal approach: joint review by activities, coordinated submission of consolidated packages, Contracting Officer participation or leadership in planning to process consolidated packages orderly through the fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with interested groups (Congress, unions, media, public)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat CITA program communications as sensitive: keep Congress advised, handle local media/community interest, and coordinate responses to public inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers must ensure they make no statements implying a decision that requires higher authority approval. FOIA inputs should be prepared closely with legal counsel and higher authority as needed (example: a 4-page FOIA request with 30+ questions requiring extensive documentation). Replies to union employees should be consistent, accurate, and supportive of general policy; written responses should be coordinated with Naval Supply Systems Command. Ultimately, replies to public inquiries remain the responsibility of the field activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer's advisory and participatory role in pre-solicitation phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer may provide assistance and professional advice in developing multifunction solicitations, consolidation, and early program planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation may occur before decision to commence cost-comparison and before receipt of purchase request. The CO's role in grouping functions is advisory but can significantly benefit functional activities; in some instances the CO may take the lead in planning consolidated solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance acquisition planning prior to receipt of purchase request
rubrics_metrics.description: Address managerial aspects of implementing new guidelines early—well before actual receipt of purchase requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider internal organization/staffing, assistance to requiring activities on SOW development and milestone planning, and the CO's role in the Task Group. Naval Material Command emphasizes timely planning and availability of procurement personnel as critical to success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structure: dedicated Services/CITA branch vs cradle-to-grave approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate internal organization options (e.g., customer-oriented branches, dedicated Services Branch, CITA program coordinator) to process service-type procurements effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Regions with dedicated Services Branches (Travis AFB, NRCO Washington) developed higher technical professionalism; NRCO Long Beach had a CITA coordinator. Cradle-to-grave (contract negotiator retains end-to-end responsibility) can preserve continuity but risks contract administration slipping under heavy new workloads. Consider feasibility given geographic dispersion and staffing levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a dedicated Contract Administration function
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider creating a separate Contract Administration Branch to relieve negotiators of post-award administration duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience indicates administration is among first areas to slip with growing backlogs. A dedicated admin staff enables scheduling/approval of pre-performance conferences, daily work plans, periodic progress meetings, surveillance plans, and monitoring of QAEs and COTRs (Travis AFB example). Air Force typically has more manpower resources to support this than Navy; geographic dispersion may impede centralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide procurement-series billets and training at receiving activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Require activities engaged in significant contracting-out to establish billets for procurement-series personnel to oversee contract administration and assist SOW preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestion: one procurement-series person per given contract dollar value, with additional billets as program grows. Example: China Lake includes GS-1102 contracting personnel as authorized billets performing administration and SOW review. Training for these personnel generally must be provided by the contracting office and may require additional procurement management staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and plan for workload impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize CITA/A-76 emphasis may significantly increase contracting office workload (processing CITA packages, Task Group participation, reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over FY80-82 over 115 functional categories to be reviewed; 45+ in FY80 alone. Solicit customer input on expected number and types of functions as a planning aid. Expect overtime, weekend work, and increased time demands to meet study milestones (Air Force experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Administrative Lead Time (PALT) standard and realistic expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: PALT = time from receipt of purchase request to award; formal goal for actions > $10,000 is 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research indicates 60-day goal is virtually impossible for many C/I support procurements due to SOW development, solicitation methods (e.g., Two-Step Formal Advertising), SBA negotiations, certification audits, and approval delays. Examples: 169 days for AudioVisual services (Two-Step FAD); 224 days for Guard Services with 8(a) set-aside requiring SOW rework and SBA negotiation. Recommendations: seek longer offer acceptance periods (75–90 days), strict adherence to milestones, and personal monitoring by the Contracting Officer to avoid adverse effects on PALT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify contracting authority and responsibility allocation (NAVSUP vs NAVFAC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine which organization is responsible for procurement of each functional category (NAVSUP, NAVFAC, or case-by-case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of 119 functions considered for FY80-82, 79 were identified for NAVSUP, 22 for NAVFAC, remainder case-by-case. For multi-function contracting, the concept of 'predominant user' determines procuring authority. NAVSUP should issue listings to NFPS activities indicating procurement responsibilities. Unclear allocations can delay resolicitations and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal training in A-76/cost-comparison processes for contracting personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure contracting staff are familiar with cost-comparison methodology and technical details needed to support CITA actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many contracting personnel lacked understanding of methods to evaluate cost-type proposals or incentive arrangements, use of options, period base (one vs three years), bid opening for negotiated solicitations, and when cost comparison is complete. A four-day Army Logistics Management Center course exists but is mainly oriented to financial management personnel; a dedicated in-house program based on current guidance is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group composition and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Task Group initiates and drives the cost-comparison process; typical membership includes functional/operational reps, Manpower/Personnel, Finance/Accounting, Legal, and Contracting Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chairperson (often Comptroller or Planning Officer in Navy; Manpower Office in Air Force) should chair meetings, oversee preparation of the in-house Government cost estimate, and maintain objectivity/integrity. The Task Group must establish realistic milestones, prepare a comprehensive SOW, develop an accurate Government cost estimate, conduct the cost comparison after bids/offers are evaluated by the Contracting Officer, and prepare Decision Summary Recommendations for Approving Authority. Success depends on early communications, detailed planning, and diligent steering of the effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer's level of involvement in Task Group
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer should assess appropriate involvement in Task Group activities while recognizing areas they should be excluded from (e.g., developing Government cost estimates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COs participate in Task Group but should avoid directly performing Government cost estimates (these are financial management responsibilities). COs provide evaluation of private-sector bids/offers and professional advice in SOW and procurement matters; they also monitor milestones and help drive the process to completion.
